item.title: Spain: 69 candles lit at Toledo Cathedral for train crash victims
item.description: Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia attended a state funeral at Toledo Cathedral on Tuesday 10 November for the 69 people killed in a devastating high-speed train collision near Urda on 28 October.

item.title: Argentina: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass before 650,000 in Córdoba
item.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass before an estimated 650,000 people in Córdoba, Argentina. The pontiff greeted crowds from his popemobile before urging worshippers to open their hearts and embrace their faith.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV draws huge crowds in Córdoba after record Buenos Aires mass
item.description: Faithful from all over Argentina, from the farthest north of the country to Patagonia in the south and points in between, drove hours to be on hand for the service led by the Pope.

item.title: Paraguay's new president vows to recover pension funds at risk in Ueno Bank crisis
item.description: Paraguay’s new president, Pedro Alliana, promises to recover pension funds affected by the intervention in Ueno Bank. The crisis, which led to the dismissal of Santiago Peña, has left up to 7,000 people unemployed in Paraguay and other countries.

item.title: Web Summit Lisbon day 2 cancelled due to Storm Charles
item.description: The technology conference closed its doors on the second day.

item.title: Energy boss Birol urges governments to accelerate global electrification at COP31
item.description: In an exclusive interview, Fatih Birol urged governments to accelerate the electrification of the global economy, as the COP31 gets underway.

item.title: Democrats took the House, Senate and a good deal of Republican pride: So who are the real winners and losers?
item.description: Democrats took the House, the Senate and a good deal of Republican pride last Tuesday night. Here is who came out ahead, and whose hangover lingers on this week.

item.title: Costa seeks to reassure Merz after EU budget ultimatum
item.description: António Costa has replied to Friedrich Merz's controversial letter linking a deal on the EU budget to a deal on Ukraine aid. Four countries have already pushed back against the German chancellor's ultimatum.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 10th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 10th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Portugal on alert as storms Bruna and Charles raise sting jet risk of 160 km/h winds
item.description: Portugal faces a high weather-risk scenario as depression Charles passes and a rare, destructive 'sting jet' could form, bringing wind gusts above 160 km/h, especially across the Greater Lisbon area.

item.title: Italian government debates aid to Kyiv while Abu Dhabi holds talks on Ukraine's future
item.description: The Italian government coalition has split over the military aid to Ukraine, just after Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni secured a seat for Rome in the peace talks session in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Russia’s ‘unfriendly countries’ list now targets property, child custody and debts
item.description: Moscow’s list of states it deems unfriendly was set in March 2022 for foreign economic policy, but decrees and court rulings now apply it to child custody, vehicle registration and debt repayment.

item.title: Belgium: Prince Harry and Meghan visit EU Parliament for child safety event
item.description: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan visited the European Parliament in Brussels, on Tuesday 10 November, to discuss the dangers children face online. The couple met families affected by online abuse before Harry addressed the gathering.

item.title: DLR, NASA and Canada plan lunar greenhouses to grow food for astronauts
item.description: What sounds like science fiction is becoming a concrete research project: the German Aerospace Center (DLR), NASA and Canada's CSA are developing a concept for lunar greenhouses.

item.title: GCC members agree to station forces at new military command post in Kuwait
item.description: The new post in Kuwait will be part of the six Gulf countries’ joint military command, based in Riyadh, GCC announced on Tuesday.

item.title: Home appliances could be next after fridge hacks, warns EU cyber chief
item.description: The warning comes after supermarkets in at least 12 European countries were hit by cyberattacks in October and November, with France the worst affected.

item.title: 'Second chance of survival': Newborn stingray takes first swim before being released back into wild
item.description: Rays are often accidentally caught in fishing nets, which can cause females to expel their eggs. This Portuguese project gives pups a second chance.

item.title: EU budget battle erupts as four countries defy Merz over Ukraine aid
item.description: Slovakia's Robert Fico accused the German chancellor of "blackmail" as four EU countries resisted his demand to link approval of the bloc's next long-term budget to fresh financial support for Ukraine.

item.title: Inside Uzbekistan's agricultural transformation: Technology, investment and food security
item.description: From higher-yield orchards to modern irrigation and digital farming, Uzbekistan is changing how its farms operate. Business Line examines the investment and support behind these developments, and the challenge of increasing exports while securing domestic food supplies.

item.title: How AI glasses are changing the way people communicate
item.description: AI glasses, more than half of which are made in China, are moving from gadget to everyday tool for travellers and people with hearing loss, as makers hope they will one day replace smartphones.

item.title: Qatar sees 'progress' in US-Iran talks after White House meeting
item.description: A day after Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met Trump at the White House, a Qatari foreign ministry spokesman said both sides were making positive statements about a diplomatic solution but that “we cannot say how close or how far away an agreement is.”

item.title: ‘Scared to death of those stairs’: Addressing the fear of falling among older adults
item.description: Falls pose a significant health risk for older adults, and the likelihood and severity of fall-related injuries increase with age. Yet many people remain unaware of the factors that contribute to falls, including anxiety, hearing loss and mobility problems.

item.title: Infineon says AI data centre boom to persist despite growing backlash
item.description: Infineon expects soaring demand for chips powering AI infrastructure to sustain growth, despite mounting concerns over the environmental and economic costs of data centre expansion.

item.title: Denmark pledges €643 million in military aid as Zelenskyy meets Nordic leaders
item.description: The Copenhagen talks coincided with the start of US-mediated negotiations between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Vodafone suffers huge net loss on Germany hit but raises full-year outlook
item.description: British mobile phone giant Vodafone on Tuesday posted a huge post-tax loss for its first half, linked primarily to a writedown in Germany, but raised its outlook with total revenue increasing.

item.title: EU pledges €10 million for Bulgarian Black Sea search, rescue operations
item.description: The EU has pledged €10 million for Bulgaria to bolster search and rescue operations in the Black Sea, which is becoming one of the most dangerous transport routes in the world due to continued drone attacks.

item.title: Central Asia's first wind farm with large-scale batteries nears completion in Uzbekistan
item.description: Twenty-five of the 26 turbines are already supplying the national grid, while the storage system undergoes safety checks. The €232m investment includes international financing and a 25-year electricity purchase agreement, as large-scale storage installations in Europe more than doubled in 2025.

item.title: Aerial footage reveals devastation after deadly Bulgaria highway crash
item.description: Drone footage shows the aftermath of a massive pile-up involving dozens of vehicles on a foggy highway near Yambol, Bulgaria, where 11 people were killed and dozens injured, according to state media.

item.title: Portugal on alert as storm Charles brings red warnings to Madeira
item.description: The government warns of flooding, falling trees and power cuts, urging people to shelter "during peaks of rain and wind". Forecasts indicate heavy rain with thunder, six-metre waves and gusts up to 130 km/h, with parts of Madeira under red alert.

item.title: Five EU countries demand UK pays for electricity market access
item.description: The leaders of Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Luxembourg and the Netherlands want Britain to contribute to EU regional development funds in return for closer energy ties, adding a new hurdle to negotiations ahead of the 20 November summit.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 10th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 10th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: EU candidates will not have a say on anti-Orbán safeguards
item.description: Montenegro is the first to test the EU's new safeguards, with member states expected to reach a position as early as next week. But contrary to the other negotiating chapters, Podgorica is finding out that the safeguards, including the possibility of suspending voting rights, are non-negotiable.

item.title: Europe must stop 'begging' for seat at Ukraine peace talks, ex-NATO chief warns
item.description: Former NATO boss Anders Fogh Rasumussen warned Europe against merely pleading to part of the US-brokered ceasefire talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, saying that securing a seat at the negotiating table comes through strength, not “begging”.

item.title: Stocks rally as investors snap up tech shares at lower prices
item.description: Stocks rallied on Tuesday, extending a technology-led surge on Wall Street, as investors took advantage of lower prices following last week's rout. Falling oil prices added to the upbeat mood.

item.title: Japan to supply Philippine military with coastal radar and drones
item.description: Tokyo says the new equipment will help Manila monitor shipping routes that are also important to Japan.

item.title: Donnie Dunagan, the Purple Heart marine who was the original voice of Disney’s Bambi, dies aged 92
item.description: Dunagan was six years old when he voiced the young deer in the classic Disney animated film. He went on to enlist in the Marine Corps and retired as a Major with three Purple Hearts.

item.title: 12 dead and dozens injured in Bulgarian motorway pile-up
item.description: Drone footage shows cars crushed between lorries in thick fog near Yambol, and the road has been closed in both directions in an incident involving over 50 vehicles.

item.title: Spain clears Ceuta port migrant camp as 300 return to Morocco
item.description: Around 5,800 people are still living in emergency facilities set up after mass arrivals in the territory at the end of July.

item.title: Trump says Iran war ‘effectively over’ as Tehran denies planned talks
item.description: Speaking after meeting Qatar’s prime minister, a key mediator, Trump said further strikes were “quite unlikely” but that the US was “locked and loaded”. Meanwhile, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei told Washington to stop “manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks”.

item.title: Inside the Japanese programme using school committees and remedial classes to improve learning in Madagascar
item.description: A programme developed by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) is tackling low literacy and school dropout in Madagascar by giving parents and communities a direct say in how schools are run.

item.title: Prince Harry blasts social media 'brainwashing' – as Brussels audience keeps scrolling
item.description: The Duke of Sussex, in Brussels, praised the EU Kids Act, the proposed law regulating how children use online services, while the Duchess stayed silent following her father’s arrest over alleged possession of child sexual abuse material.

item.title: Macron wants AI banned wherever it threatens children
item.description: The French president made the comments as the country draws up a charter to protect its citizens from threats posed by artificial intelligence.

item.title: More computing power, more jobs? Denmark boosts its AI supercomputer
item.description: The 500 million DKK (approximately €67 million) investment in Denmark’s AI supercomputer could help create businesses and jobs and enable public institutions to use AI securely, according to Tuesday’s announcement.

item.title: 'She owns everything': Portugal's last circus elephant adapts to life of freedom in new sanctuary
item.description: Another elephant from a circus in Belgium is expected to arrive at the sanctuary as early as November.

item.title: Meghan Markle makes first public appearance since father's arrest
item.description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived in Brussels for an event highlighting the dangers of online harm to children. Meghan's appearance marks her first public engagement since her father, Thomas Markle Sr., was charged with possessing child sexual abuse material in the US.

item.title: French pupils step up protests as government concessions fall flat
item.description: Unions walked out of talks with the prime minister’s office over the presence of the far right, while firework mortars have been set off inside schools as tensions rise.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia reportedly show 'a little bit of flexibility' on territory as Abu Dhabi talks begin
item.description: The renewed US-mediated negotiations come amid deep divisions over territorial concessions and post-war security guarantees, with European leaders pressing for a role in discussions that could reshape the continent's security.

item.title: Trump vows to back Pete Hegseth as Republican lawmaker pushes impeachment vote
item.description: Republican Congressman Thomas Massie is seeking to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging military action against Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation.

item.title: EPSO: Italian applicant boom puts EU hiring balance to the test
item.description: The EPSO generalist exam started on November 9, but almost half of the applicants come from one single country, Italy. This clashes with the Commission's own hiring rules, which favour 'underrepresented countries' to address geographical staff imbalances.

item.title: Senegal: Footage reveals wreckage of deadly migrant boat in which 39 people died
item.description: At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat sank off Senegal's Atlantic coast. Footage shows the shattered vessel washed ashore as rescuers continue searching for victims.
